reconstruction.text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive commutative group structure and a measurable structure satisfying BorelSpace. Let V:E -> R be C^2. Let alpha,beta be nonnegative real numbers, with alpha>0 and alpha<=beta, and let eta>0 satisfy beta*eta<=1. For every x,v in E assume
  alpha*||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= beta*||v||^2,
where D^2 V is the iterated real Frechet derivative appearing in the proposition. These are all caller-supplied mathematical hypotheses.

Define mu as the normalized exponential tilt of volume by -V. Define J as the pushforward of mu times the standard Gaussian on E under (x,z) -> (x,x+sqrt(eta)*z). Thus J is a law on E x E, whose coordinates will be denoted (x,y). Define nu as the second marginal of J. Define Lambda as the pushforward of J under (x,y) -> (y,2*x-y), and F(x,y)=(x,2*x-y). Write H=L^2(J;R) and K=L^2(nu;R), with functions understood as almost-everywhere classes. Let mY be the sigma algebra on E x E pulled back from E by the second coordinate. Let HP be the closed mY-measurable subspace of H. Let P:H -> H be conditional expectation onto that sigma algebra followed by inclusion in H. The measurable-space comparison required to define it is internally supplied. Let M:K -> H be the real-linear isometric pullback along the second coordinate, so M u is represented by (x,y) -> u(y).

The conclusion first asserts that mu, J and nu are probability measures; that HP equals the range of the linear map underlying P; and that P fixes each element of HP.

There are jointly chosen witnesses S,e,U,T,Gamma,q,GammaP0,Inv,A0,B0,V0,R as described below. All are conclusions depending on the caller data, not further premises. Their order of introduction permits dependence on preceding witnesses. They are common witnesses for all the later universally quantified observables; they are not chosen afresh for each such observable.

S is a Markov kernel from E to E. For EVERY y in E its measure S(y) is exactly the normalized exponential tilt of volume by
  x -> -V((y+x)/2) - ||y-x||^2/(8*eta).
It is a conditional kernel for Lambda, namely the conditional law of the second coordinate given the first, and both marginals of Lambda equal nu. The every-y equality of measures is stronger in scope than a merely nu-almost-everywhere description of the kernel.

e:K -> HP is a surjective real-linear isometry (an isometric linear equivalence), and for every u in K its inclusion into H equals M u. U:H -> H is a real-linear isometry whose representative action for each g in H is U g = g composed with F, J-almost everywhere. U is involutive and its bounded linear map is selfadjoint. The exceptional null set in the displayed representative equality may depend on g.

T:K -> K is bounded real-linear and selfadjoint. For every u in K, simultaneously,
  ||T u|| <= ||u||,
  T u(y) = integral u(x) dS(y)(x), for nu-almost every y,
  integral T u dnu = integral u dnu.
The kernel-action equality is an equality of representatives almost everywhere for each observable u; a single common exceptional set for all u is not asserted.

Define A:HP -> HP by orthogonally projecting U restricted to HP back onto HP. Define B:HP -> H by (I-P) U P after inclusion of HP into H. Then
  A = e T e^(-1),
  A is selfadjoint, and ||A f|| <= ||f|| for every f in HP,
  P(B f)=0 for every f in HP.
Here and below multiplication of endomorphisms is composition, adjoints are Hilbert adjoints, and all operator equalities are exact equalities of bounded linear maps.

Gamma:K -> K is bounded real-linear, positive, satisfies Gamma^2=I-T^2, and commutes with T. Positivity includes selfadjointness and nonnegative quadratic form. Set GammaP=e Gamma e^(-1):HP -> HP. Then GammaP is positive, GammaP^2=I-A^2, GammaP commutes with A, and B^* B=GammaP^2 as operators on HP.

q is an element of K represented nu-almost everywhere by the constant function 1. It satisfies T q=q, and for every u in K,
  <q,u> = integral u dnu.
Put qP=e q and HP0={f in HP: <qP,f>=0}. It has internally inherited complete real Hilbert structures. For every f in HP,
  f belongs to HP0 if and only if integral (e^(-1) f) dnu=0.
Furthermore GammaP qP=0. Set
  gamma = 2*sqrt(alpha*eta)/(1+alpha*eta).
The conclusion asserts gamma>0.

GammaP0:HP0 -> HP0 is a bounded restriction of GammaP: for every f in HP0, inclusion(GammaP0 f)=GammaP(inclusion f). It is positive and GammaP0-gamma*I is positive. It is a unit in the algebra of bounded endomorphisms of HP0. There is a bounded real-linear Inv:HP0 -> HP0 for which
  Inv GammaP0=I, GammaP0 Inv=I, ||Inv||<=1/gamma,
  Inv is selfadjoint.
This is the SAME two-sided inverse of the SAME restricted operator throughout the subsequent conclusions. No corresponding positive lower bound or bounded inverse for GammaP on all of HP is asserted; indeed the stated constant vector is annihilated there.

A0:HP0 -> HP0 is a bounded restriction of A. For every u in HP0 its inclusion is A applied to the inclusion of u. It is selfadjoint, commutes with GammaP0, satisfies A0^2+GammaP0^2=I, and commutes with Inv.

Let Hperp=ker P, which is a closed complete real Hilbert subspace of H. Membership in Hperp means zero conditional expectation under P, not merely zero total J-integral. B0:HP0 -> Hperp is a bounded restriction of B, meaning its inclusion into H equals B on the inclusion of every f in HP0. V0:HP0 -> Hperp is bounded real-linear and satisfies
  V0=B0 Inv, B0=V0 GammaP0,
  V0^* V0=I on HP0,
  ||V0 f||=||f|| for every f in HP0.
V0 is therefore asserted to be an isometric embedding into Hperp. Neither surjectivity onto Hperp nor V0 V0^*=I on Hperp is stated.

R:H -> Hperp is a bounded real-linear map whose inclusion into H is g-P g for every g in H. For EVERY g in H the ambient adjoint of B satisfies
  B^* g = inclusion_HP0_into_HP(B0^*(R g)).
Thus this adjoint identity has the whole ambient joint L^2 space as its input domain, not just Hperp or a range of V0.

Define D:Hperp -> Hperp by D=R U inclusion_Hperp_into_H. For every h in Hperp its inclusion in H equals U h-P(U h). The operator identity
  V0^* D = - A0 V0^*
holds on ALL of Hperp. The proposition does not restrict this identity to the range of V0.

Finally, for every f in H satisfying integral f dJ=0, there exists fP in HP0 whose inclusion into HP equals the conditional expectation condExpL2(f). Set fperp=R f in Hperp and fV=V0^* fperp in HP0. Then
  B^*(inclusion fperp)=inclusion_HP0_into_HP(GammaP0 fV),
  inclusion_HP0_into_HP(GammaP0 fV)=GammaP(inclusion_HP0_into_HP fV),
  ||f||^2=||fP||^2+||fperp||^2,
  ||fV||<=||fperp||.
Define the actual output g=U(P f-(f-P f)) in H. Its total J-integral is zero. There exists gP in HP0 whose inclusion into HP equals condExpL2(g). Set gperp=R g and gV=V0^* gperp. For these actual conditional and adjoint components of that output, the conclusion asserts
  gP=A0 fP-GammaP0 fV,
  gV=GammaP0 fP+A0 fV,
  ||gP||^2+||gV||^2=||fP||^2+||fV||^2.
The expressions on the right do not define gP and gV: their independent identification as components of g is part of the conclusion. The mean-zero condition is a premise on f only; mean zero of g is a conclusion. The per-f witnesses fP and gP occur after f is quantified and do not change the earlier common operators.

All integral and representative statements use the measures explicitly stated above. All spaces and subspaces are real, including their inner products and bounded linear maps. The explicit lower-bound and inverse constants depend only on alpha and eta through gamma; beta enters the initial Hessian and step-size assumptions and does not occur in gamma. There is no further numerical dimension factor, higher-derivative assumption, additional caller-supplied kernel or spectral hypothesis, asserted onto statement for V0, asserted inverse on the whole HP, or asserted contraction rate for the final output in this proposition.
